title: Postquant Labs Launches Quip Virtual Machine to Unify Quantum Execution Across Hardware Architectures - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Postquant Labs launched the Quip Virtual Machine, an EVM-inspired runtime spanning annealers, gate-based and classical hardware with a gas-based cost model, plus first quantum smart contracts on the Aglais testnet. A 1,930-trial D-Wave vs simulated annealing portfolio benchmark showed the annealer matching or beating the classical solver every time, with a 2.56% median objective improvement.

insights.claim: Postquant Labs launched the Quip Virtual Machine (QVM), modeled conceptually on the Ethereum Virtual Machine, with a constraint-based programming language and runtime designed to unify execution across annealers, gate-based quantum systems and classical hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Blockchain-style execution layers are being tried as a hardware-agnostic abstraction for quantum.
insights.locator: Quantum computing marketplace developer Postquant Labs

insights.claim: The QVM uses a gas-based cost model that prices quantum operations by qubit space, run duration and entanglement metrics, quoting a maximum compute cost in shared credits before execution.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Upfront deterministic pricing addresses a major barrier to enterprise quantum procurement.
insights.locator: The platform introduces a gas-based cost model

insights.claim: In a 1,930-trial head-to-head during Quantum.Tech World on 28-asset portfolios with 500-read budgets, a D-Wave Advantage annealer matched or beat classical simulated annealing in every trial, winning 970 races and tying 960.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A vendor-run benchmark with ties counted as non-losses; treat as supportive but not independent proof of advantage.
insights.locator: To evaluate performance on live workloads

insights.claim: The quantum annealer's median portfolio objective quality improvement was 2.56%, and against exact solver Gurobi the QPU recovered certified-optimal selections on 20- and 28-name portfolios while simulated annealing lagged 1.2% to 4.4% behind the optimum.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small-problem results; relevance to larger production portfolios is unproven.
insights.locator: To evaluate performance on live workloads

insights.claim: Every QVM computation passes a three-tier verification architecture that cross-checks quantum outputs against classical simulations, benchmarks results independently and binds execution records to specific hardware with cryptographic attestations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Verifiability of quantum outputs is a prerequisite for decentralized quantum marketplaces.
insights.locator: Every computation executed through the QVM

insights.claim: Postquant Labs plans to move the QVM from the Aglais testnet to mainnet, where workloads will settle in native tokens via the QuipSwap protocol.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A token-settled quantum compute marketplace adds crypto exposure; no mainnet date is given.

insights.claim: Monash University, the University of Notre Dame and Purdue University are evaluating the runtime, while industrial optimization firm SiC Systems is testing the stack for AI-driven chemical and biological process modeling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Early adopters are academic and pilot-stage, with no disclosed revenue.
